text: Your Claude Code loops, working together and keeping you in the conversation. Spool makes it easy to create, manage, and talk to persistent Claude Code loops. Give them work, let them coordinate, and stay involved through chat. Less switching between sessions and carrying messages between loops. More time deciding what they should work on and reviewing what they produce. Spool is pre-1.0 and developed in the open by a fleet of Claude Code loops and their operator. The four loops in this repo's issues and PRs run on Spool, building Spool. Commits are co-authored by the model that wrote them; every change lands through a pull request that CI gates and a reviewer reads, and the operator is the one who merges it. Found a problem? CONTRIBUTING.md says how to report it and who answers. You need Linux, macOS or Windows with WSL2 , with Docker running, git , Go 1.25+, Node 20.19+ or 22.12+, and Claude Code on a Claude subscription (only to make a token in step 3). Get Spool and build it. git clone https://github.com/enes-alatas/spool && cd spool make build image That builds bin/spool , the control room inside it, and the two Docker images a loop runs in. Start it and sign in. Run ./bin/spool . On its first start it prints a one-time password for the user admin . Open http://127.0.0.1:8080 , sign in as admin with that password, and choose your own. Missed the password? ./bin/spool user reset admin prints a new one. The control room opens on Set up your fleet : three cards, in the order below. Each checks itself and turns done on its own. Harness. Run claude setup-token , then choose Add token on the card and paste what it printed. Your loops run on your Claude plan through it. Loops. Choose New loop , and give it a name and a mission. Its first wake builds its workstation, which takes a minute or two the first time; the card is done when that wake's first turn ends. Chat surface. Choose Attach a bot , then Attach Telegram or Attach Slack . Then choose Get a link code , send the code to your bot in a direct message, and reply YES when it asks. That links your account and makes you the loop's owner. Message the bot once more: the card is done when the loop answers you there. No chat app? You can talk to a loop on its page in the control room instead. Once the Harness and Loops cards are done, choose Skip for now on the Chat surface card to finish the setup page without one, and attach a bot later on the loop's page. docs/CONTAINMENT.md has the whole picture, including what containment does not do. SECURITY.md says how to report a vulnerability. A loop starts with the control room only. Attach a bot to reach it from Telegram or Slack too: each loop is its own bot or app, and step 5 of the quick start attaches the first one. docs/TELEGRAM.md covers BotFather, groups and reactions; docs/SLACK.md covers the app manifest, the two tokens, reactions and polls. Spool keeps a sender allowlist , and only people on it reach your loops. Anyone else who messages one of your bots is ignored: their message never reaches a loop, they can't bind a group, and /spool_status won't answer them. Linking your account in step 5 put you on it. To let someone else in, add them as a user ( spool user add , or Settings → Users and access ) and have them link theirs under Settings → Link Telegram or Link Slack . Settings → Users and access lists each user's links and can block a user on every bot, along with anyone an old pairing code allowed without a user; a blocked sender gets no reply at all. A Slack app is already private to the workspace you install it in, and the allowlist applies there too. Loop-to-loop traffic is internal and unaffected. spool --help lists every flag. spool token prints the operator token again. make server # Go binary only (uses last-built UI) make dev # run backend on :8080 make ui-dev # vite dev server with /api proxy make test # tier 1: unit + architecture tests make itest # tier 2: real binary vs fakeclaude (protocol fake), ~10min # (~7min without a docker daemon; two files skip) make image # build the spool-workstation and spool-egress images locally make lint # gofmt + vet (as Linux and as macOS) + golangci-lint make e2e-m1 # tier 3: real claude sessions (spends plan tokens) Testing is three-tiered (see docs/QUALITY.md ): unit and fakeclaude-backed integration tests gate every PR in CI; the real-claude e2e suites ( scripts/e2e/ ) run locally per milestone: session resume across process death and orchestrator restarts (m1), tick scheduling and trailer clamping (m2), mention relay + storm guard (m4), Telegram (m5), worktree isolation (m6).
